title: Climate Summit Faces 'Ghost' Warning as Fossil Fuel Mentions Disappear
subtitle: Negotiators at COP31 struggle to reach a final agreement as key promises on energy and finance are removed from official documents.

summary.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey is facing a major crisis after draft agreements removed all mentions of fossil fuels. Campaigners and some nations are criticizing the move, calling the event a 'ghost summit' that lacks real action. Panama has threatened to block the final outcome unless their demands for stronger climate commitments are met. Meanwhile, discussions regarding financial support for developing nations remain stalled. The summit is now in its final hours, with leaders under heavy pressure to restore meaningful goals.
summary.zh: 在土耳其舉行的 COP31 氣候峰會因協議草案刪除所有關於化石燃料的內容而面臨重大危機。倡議人士與部分國家批評此舉，稱此次會議為缺乏實質行動的「幽靈峰會」。巴拿馬已威脅，除非其對更強有力氣候承諾的要求獲得滿足，否則將阻擋最終結果。與此同時，關於開發中國家財政支持的討論仍陷入僵局。峰會正進入最後階段，各國領袖正面臨恢復實質目標的巨大壓力。

paragraphs.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey is currently facing a serious crisis as it enters its final hours. Negotiators are struggling to reach a deal after a new draft of the main agreement removed all mentions of fossil fuels. This change has caused anger among climate activists and several participating nations, who fear the summit will fail to produce any real progress in the fight against global warming.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其舉行的第 31 屆聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）正進入最後階段，卻面臨嚴重危機。由於主要協議的最新草案刪除了所有關於化石燃料的內容，談判代表們正陷入難以達成共識的困境。此舉引發了氣候倡議人士與多個與會國家的憤怒，他們擔心這場峰會將無法在對抗全球暖化的行動中取得任何實質進展。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the second draft of the agreement was released on Thursday afternoon. It significantly weakened goals related to moving away from fossil fuels and reduced support for developing countries that need help dealing with extreme weather. Critics have labeled the event a “ghost summit,” suggesting that if the current text remains, the meeting will have no meaningful results to show the world.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，該協議的第二版草案於週四下午發布。草案大幅削弱了與淘汰化石燃料相關的目標，並減少了對需要協助應對極端氣候的開發中國家的支持。批評者將此次會議稱為「幽靈峰會」，認為若維持目前的文本，這場會議將無法向世界展現任何具備實質意義的成果。

paragraphs.en: Panama has taken a strong stand against the new draft. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, sent a letter to the presidents of the summit, who represent Australia and Turkey. In the letter, Panama announced that it would block any final agreement unless its demands for stronger action are met. Navarro argued that while leaders have given many “beautiful speeches,” the planet is being destroyed and the world expects radical change that the current negotiations are failing to deliver.
paragraphs.zh: 巴拿馬對這份新草案採取了強硬立場。該國環境部長納瓦洛（Juan Carlos Navarro）致函給代表澳洲與土耳其的峰會主席團。巴拿馬在信中宣布，除非其對於採取更強有力行動的要求獲得滿足，否則將阻擋任何最終協議的通過。納瓦洛主張，儘管各國領袖發表了許多「動聽的演說」，但地球正遭到破壞，世界期待的是激進的變革，而目前的談判卻未能達成此目標。

paragraphs.en: Many experts believe that the summit is at a dangerous point. Because COP negotiations require a consensus—an agreement where all countries must agree—the position taken by Panama could stop the entire process. Mohamed Adow, director of the Power Shift Africa thinktank, noted that the talks have been “muzzled” by countries that produce fossil fuels and do not want to commit to a transition away from them.
paragraphs.zh: 許多專家認為峰會正處於危險關頭。由於氣候大會的談判需要達成共識，即所有國家必須一致同意，因此巴拿馬的立場可能會導致整個進程停擺。非洲能源轉型智庫「能源轉型非洲」（Power Shift Africa）主任阿多（Mohamed Adow）指出，談判過程已被那些生產化石燃料且不願承諾轉型的國家所「封殺」。

paragraphs.en: Financial support for poorer nations remains another major point of disagreement. Campaigners argue that wealthy nations are failing to provide the money needed for developing countries to adapt to climate change. Rachitaa Gupta, from the Global Campaign to Demand Climate Justice, described this as a “moral bankruptcy” of the global north. She stated that the cause of the climate crisis is clear, but the political will to pay for the solution is missing.
paragraphs.zh: 對貧窮國家的財政支持是另一個主要的分歧點。倡議人士認為，富裕國家未能提供開發中國家適應氣候變遷所需的資金。來自「氣候正義需求全球運動」（Global Campaign to Demand Climate Justice）的古普塔（Rachitaa Gupta）將此形容為全球北方國家的「道德破產」。她表示，氣候危機的成因顯而易見，但為解決方案買單的政治意願卻付之闕如。

paragraphs.en: Despite the frustration, some observers are looking for other signs of progress. John Verdieck, Director of International Climate Policy at The Nature Conservancy, noted that while the removal of fossil fuel language is a major step backward, work continues on other fronts. He pointed to initiatives like Brazil’s plan to stop deforestation as areas where positive change might still happen outside of the main text.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管感到挫折，仍有一些觀察家在尋找其他進展的跡象。大自然保護協會（The Nature Conservancy）國際氣候政策主任維迪克（John Verdieck）指出，雖然刪除化石燃料相關文字是一大倒退，但在其他方面的工作仍在持續。他舉例，巴西提出的停止森林砍伐計畫，就是可能在主要文本之外實現正面變革的領域。

paragraphs.en: Inside the summit, the atmosphere remains tense. The joint presidencies of Australia and Turkey have been criticized for shrinking the original 18-page draft by half, cutting out many commitments that vulnerable countries were relying on. Chris Bowen, the president of the COP31 negotiations, has defended the process, claiming that countries like China are engaging in a spirit of “positive engagement” despite the difficult debates. However, this has done little to calm the activists who feel that the summit is ignoring the defining challenge of our time.
paragraphs.zh: 峰會內部的氣氛依然緊張。澳洲與土耳其的聯合主席團因將原本 18 頁的草案刪減了一半，並刪除了許多脆弱國家所依賴的承諾而受到批評。COP31 談判主席鮑文（Chris Bowen）為此過程辯護，聲稱儘管辯論艱難，但像中國這樣的國家仍展現了「積極參與」的精神。然而，這並未平息倡議人士的怒火，他們認為峰會忽視了當代最關鍵的挑戰。

paragraphs.en: As the final hours approach, the future of the COP31 agreement remains uncertain. The summit was intended to help meet the goals of the Paris agreement, which aims to limit temperature rises and protect the planet from the worst effects of climate change. Instead, negotiators are now caught in a difficult situation, trying to balance the interests of fossil fuel-producing nations with the urgent demands of those most affected by the climate crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著最後時刻逼近，COP31 協議的未來仍充滿不確定性。此次峰會旨在協助達成《巴黎協定》（Paris Agreement）的目標，該協定致力於限制氣溫上升，並保護地球免受氣候變遷最嚴重的影響。然而，談判代表們現在陷入了兩難，試圖在化石燃料生產國的利益與受氣候危機影響最深地區的迫切需求之間取得平衡。

paragraphs.en: For many, the situation at COP31 is a test of political responsibility. Andreas Sieber, of the campaign group 350.org, called the current lack of leadership “utterly embarrassing.” He argued that the presidencies have reduced one of the most important issues in the world to a small paragraph that they would rather delete than address. As the world watches, the question remains whether the leaders in Turkey can find a way to move past their disagreements and deliver a result that actually addresses the climate emergency.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多人而言，COP31 的局勢是對政治責任的一場考驗。倡議組織「350.org」的席伯（Andreas Sieber）稱目前缺乏領導力的情況「極其丟臉」。他主張，主席團將世界上最重要的議題之一縮減為一個他們寧可刪除也不願處理的小段落。在全世界的注視下，土耳其的領袖們能否找到方法克服分歧，並提出真正能解決氣候緊急狀態的成果，仍是一個未知數。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To prevent something from happening or moving forward.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：Panama announced that it would block any final agreement unless its demands for stronger action are met.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To prevent someone or something from speaking freely or expressing opinions.
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意是給動物戴上「口套」，這裡比喻壓制談判進程。文中：noted that the talks have been “muzzled” by countries that produce fossil fuels and do not want to commit to a transition away from them.

常見指天氣（鋒面）或建築正面，這裡指不同的活動領域。文中：John Verdieck, Director of International Climate Policy at The Nature Conservancy, noted that while the removal of fossil fuel language is a major step backward, work continues on other fronts.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To make something smaller in size or amount.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指物體變小，這裡指縮減文件內容。文中：The joint presidencies of Australia and Turkey have been criticized for shrinking the original 18-page draft by half, cutting out many commitments that vulnerable countries were relying on.

quiz.question: What specific action did the environment minister of Panama take regarding the new draft of the COP31 agreement?

options.A: He publicly resigned from the summit to protest the lack of progress.
options.B: He sent a formal letter to the summit presidents threatening to block the final deal.
options.C: He requested a meeting with leaders from China to discuss fossil fuel production.
options.D: He demanded that the original 18-page draft be reinstated in its entirety.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，巴拿馬環境部長 Juan Carlos Navarro 致信給代表澳洲與土耳其的峰會主席，明確表示除非其要求獲得滿足，否則巴拿馬將阻擋任何最終協議。選項 A 錯誤，因為文中並未提到他辭職；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未指名與中國開會；選項 D 雖然提到對草案不滿，但文中並未明確要求「完整恢復」18 頁草案，而是要求更強力的氣候行動。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why is Panama's opposition particularly significant to the outcome of the summit?

options.A: Panama is the largest financial contributor to the COP31 climate fund.
options.B: The summit rules require every participating nation to agree for a deal to pass.
options.C: Panama has the support of all other nations to lead the negotiations.
options.D: The summit organizers have already decided to follow Panama's advice.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，COP 談判需要「共識」（consensus），即所有國家都必須同意才能達成協議。因此，巴拿馬的反對立場具有否決權，足以阻礙整個程序。選項 A 文中未提及巴拿馬是最大金主；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到其他國家都支持巴拿馬；選項 D 錯誤，事實上組織者正因草案內容與巴拿馬立場衝突而陷入危機。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word "muzzled" most likely mean in the context of the climate talks?

options.A: Silenced or prevented from speaking freely.
options.B: Encouraged to participate in a debate.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到談判被「muzzled」（被摀住嘴），是因為化石燃料生產國不希望承諾轉型，因此限制了談判的實質內容。此處用「muzzled」來比喻談判過程受到阻礙，無法自由討論。選項 B 與文意相反；選項 C 與安全措施無關；選項 D 雖然談判困難，但「muzzled」強調的是「無法發聲」而非「感到困惑」。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding the COP31 summit?

options.A: The summit has successfully achieved its goals thanks to the cooperation of China and Australia.
options.B: Climate activists have successfully convinced all nations to stop using fossil fuels.
options.C: The summit is facing a crisis because of disagreements over fossil fuel language and financial support.
options.D: The summit is mainly focused on deforestation in Brazil rather than global climate policies.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文核心在於描述 COP31 陷入危機，特別是關於移除化石燃料相關文字以及缺乏對開發中國家的資金援助，導致各國與活動人士產生嚴重分歧。選項 A 與事實相反，談判正陷入僵局；選項 B 錯誤，化石燃料語言反而被刪除；選項 D 錯誤，巴西的造林計畫僅是文中提到的其中一個小點，並非峰會的主軸。
